# Changelog

Every stable NeoTrade desktop release, newest first.

Downloads for the current version: [latest release](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/latest).

## 0.1.12 — 2026-09-07

**New features**

- **Install a skill by pasting a link in chat**: send the assistant a skill-marketplace share link (or a skill name) and say "install" — the skill is installed directly, with no manual steps on the Skills page. Only links from the official skill marketplace are accepted; every other source is rejected. Outside Auto mode a confirmation card is shown first.
- **Publish your own skills in one click**: once a skill created in chat is installed, a share card appears; one click publishes it to the skill marketplace and copies the share link. The Skills page gains a "My skills" tab where publishing, copying the link and deleting all live.
- **Clear provenance**: skills installed from the marketplace are labelled "From marketplace" and only offer "copy share link"; the "Publish" button is reserved for skills you created or uploaded locally.
- **A settlement ledger for every bet**: after settlement, each bet is recorded as a win or a loss, and the actual hit rate is broken down by entry price band, position size, topic and more, then compared against the win rate implied by the entry price — no more reconciling by hand in the exchange back office.
- **Strategy coach**: a new "coach" role periodically reviews an agent's performance from the settlement ledger and fine-tunes the parameters of its bound strategy. You authorize it per agent: in suggest mode every parameter change raises a card and waits for your approval; only in auto mode does it take effect unattended. The coach can only adjust parameters the strategy declares — it cannot place orders, switch strategies or touch fund limits.
- **New "Active" view on the Skills page**: the Skills tab is now split into "Authorized" and "Active" views. "Active" shows the strategy the agent is actually running (self-evolved versions are marked), the strategy's three states, and the specific reason each add-on skill is not in effect (not installed, disabled globally, unavailable on this machine), so a skill can no longer go missing silently. You can also open the runtime config file in your local editor with one click to inspect parameters.
- **Logs are no longer hidden**: the log page moves from the "tap the version number seven times in Settings" easter egg to a regular settings panel, with per-agent filtering, newest entries on top, and auto-refresh every 3 seconds to follow along.

**Improvements**

- **Context menu in text fields**: right-clicking in the chat box and other text fields no longer opens the system menu; only Cut, Copy, Paste and Delete are offered, greyed out automatically according to the current state.
- **Fills show which market they belong to**: when an event has several sub-markets (for example several lines on one game), orders and fills now show "event name / sub-market name" instead of several identical titles. The market link also now opens a real page instead of a 404.
- **Settled markets are no longer missing from P&L**: realized P&L now includes positions closed by settlement, and the earnings page labels how complete the figure is (full / partial / none), so a trade is no longer dropped just because the exchange pruned an old position.
- **Share links identify the author**: skill share links now use the "@author/skill-name" format. Previously a link to a skill with a shared name resolved to whichever was published first; now it points precisely at that author's skill.
- **One Stop button**: "Stop" and "Sell all & stop" at the top of the Agents page are merged into a single "Stop" button that opens a menu to choose "Stop only" or "Sell all & stop", each spelling out its effect on open positions. With no positions it remains a one-click stop.
- **A more visible self-evolution toggle**: the self-evolution button at the top of the Agents page becomes a sparkle button — light background with an outline and grey text by default, switching to a glossy, glowing deep-teal background with white text when on, so it is obvious at a glance whether the coach is working.
- **Self-evolved versions can be published too**: on an agent's Skills page, self-evolved versions can now be uploaded to the skill marketplace and their share link copied, just like any other local skill. Old copies that still carry a wallet address from early builds must first be migrated with the wallet unlocked before publishing is allowed.
- **Live trading entry deferred**: the live-trading switch at the top temporarily shows a "Coming soon" notice; this version focuses on paper trading. Switching back to paper is unaffected.
- **New NeoTrade Terms of Service**: the full agreement can be read during the informed-consent step on first launch and under Settings → Application. It applies to all use and is independent of the three optional data-sharing consents, so it has no checkbox. Currently available in English only.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed an agent possibly betting repeatedly on the same market, or even unintentionally backing both sides at once: markets with an open order are no longer re-evaluated, and when positions cannot be read the round is skipped instead of let through.
- In an agent's authorized skills list, marketplace skills no longer wrongly show a "Publish" icon; they offer "copy share link" instead.
- Fixed the upload (publish) icon on an agent's Skills page reverting to "Upload" after switching to the "Active" view and back — the published state is now kept and the icon stays as "Share".
- The "cannot be bound as a strategy" hint line on skill cards has been removed; when binding fails, the bind dialog still gives the specific reason.
- When buying credit with an insufficient wallet balance, the app now says "Insufficient balance" and names the paying wallet and the token required, instead of showing a raw one-line error with on-chain atomic units.

[Downloads for 0.1.12](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.12)

## 0.1.11 — 2026-08-28

**New features**

- **Research right in chat**: the assistant can now search the web and read sources directly in the conversation to help you analyze market information.
- **The assistant asks you questions**: when a decision is yours to make, the assistant shows a choice card you answer with one click, instead of typing descriptions back and forth.
- **Guided strategy creation**: a new strategy-authoring wizard. Whether you only want to tweak an existing strategy, already have a complete idea, or would rather be led step by step, chat produces a working strategy one step at a time and flags mistakes on the spot.
- **Local file read/write**: the assistant can read local files and save notes, reports and similar content to a folder you choose. Every write needs your confirmation, one at a time, and can only go to directories you have explicitly authorized; the full content to be saved is shown before writing.
- **Smoother authorization**: if the folder is not yet authorized when saving a file, a folder picker opens directly; choosing one authorizes it and continues automatically, with no trip to Settings.

**Improvements**

- **Honest loading states**: pages no longer show "No data" while loading, and a failed read is reported clearly, so an account no longer looks empty by mistake.
- **Version at a glance**: the current version number is shown at the bottom of the sidebar, with an update notice when a new version is available.
- **Redeemable assets stand out**: the redeem entry for settled positions moves from a deeply nested dialog onto the page itself, so there are no more "invisible funds waiting to be claimed".
- **Chat is no longer cut off midway**: the default daily chat-usage cap is removed, so long conversations can keep going (usage stats remain visible; trading safety limits are completely unchanged).
- **Cleaner strategy switching**: after changing an agent's strategy, the old one is unbound automatically, so old and new never coexist and interfere.

**Bug fixes**

- Strategy parameter ranges can now be looked up in advance, and invalid values are reported all at once instead of through trial and error.
- Fixed several stability issues. The installers are now Apple Developer ID signed and notarized, so downloads open directly on macOS.

[Downloads for 0.1.11](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.11)

## 0.1.10 — 2026-08-27

**New features**

- **Invite codes, both directions**: the profile card now shows the invite code this install hands out, with a copy button, and takes the code you were handed. Once an inviter is recorded the card shows who it was instead of a field that can no longer be used, and re-entering a code is reported as nothing changed rather than as an error.
- **Invite code during first run**: the credit step of the setup wizard now asks for an invite code by default, with the redemption code one click away, so a new operator no longer has to finish setup and go hunting for the profile card to record who invited them.
- **Points history**: the profile card can now open the entries behind the points figure — the most recent awards across every wallet on this install, newest first, each labelled with what earned it, whether that is a credit top-up, a usage rebate, an invite reward or trading volume on a venue.

**Improvements**

- **Signed and notarised macOS builds**: this is the first release carrying a Developer ID signature and Apple notarisation, so macOS opens it without the unidentified-developer warning.
- **Chat target and approval mode in one strip**: both now sit under the message box instead of in the header, and the built-in assistant is called neotrade rather than supervisor. The approval control is a two-option menu that states what each choice does — including that skill installs and orders always ask, whichever you pick.
- **Interface size is a slider**: all three steps are visible on one track instead of hidden in a menu, and the two larger steps have been pushed further apart so they actually read as bigger.
- **Settings use the full window**: panels, notices and paragraphs no longer stop halfway across a wide window, and two notices of the same kind no longer render one wide and one narrow on the same screen.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed the app being unable to reach its own services — points, models and billing — on a machine running a tunnelled proxy or VPN that answers every lookup with a synthetic address: those addresses are no longer mistaken for a private network, and the app's own hosts stay reachable whatever address range is in use.
- Fixed renaming or hiding an agent taking several seconds to show up in the sidebar, which read as the app having dropped the edit; the list now refreshes as soon as the change lands.
- Fixed switches in Settings, Account and agent configuration responding only to a click directly on the knob — the whole switch is now clickable.
- Fixed the deposit address on the wallet screen being labelled as a payer address, which made it read as a second, different address.

[Downloads for 0.1.10](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.10)

## 0.1.9 — 2026-08-25

**New features**

- **Chat with your agents**: a new conversation panel talks to any single agent, or to a supervisor that can see the whole fleet — ask what an agent is holding, why it passed on a market, or what the fleet's P&L is, keeping a separate thread per topic. A message you send now takes priority over the agent's scheduled work, so you are no longer left waiting behind a long judgment run.
- **Encrypted backup and restore**: one passphrase-protected file captures everything a recovery phrase cannot bring back — agents and their settings, order and message history, the risk ledgers, strategy notebooks, agent memory and installed skills — and restores onto a fresh install. The factory reset now tells you whether a backup exists, and when it was taken, before it wipes anything.
- **Retire an agent instead of deleting it**: hiding an agent shuts it down completely but keeps its record and its wallet, so it can be brought back later with its history intact. A permanent delete is still there when you want one, and every agent can now carry a name of your own.
- **History follows the wallet**: decision history and conversations are keyed to the wallet address rather than to the agent, so deleting and recreating an agent — or re-importing the same recovery phrase — brings that wallet's past back instead of opening on an empty console.
- **Ask for a market by its link**: paste a market's page link or its slug into chat and the agent can now resolve it to the real market, with its close time and both outcomes, instead of having no way to act on a market you named.
- **Agents can read their own realized profit**: an agent asked what it has made now reports realized, unrealized and total figures from the same recorded series the Overview chart draws, and the supervisor can do it for every agent at once. Settled winners no longer read as zero, and an agent with no recorded figures says so rather than reporting a false zero.
- **An agent can adopt a playbook from chat**: an agent that has drafted and installed a strategy can now ask to bind it, and to add it to its own permitted list — each behind an approval card showing the change, the skill's files and scripts, and any money-moving tools it declares, with the binding card also naming how many positions you have open.
- **Market data on restricted networks**: where Polymarket's own hosts cannot be reached from your network, market reads switch automatically to a hosted route at start-up, so a fresh install behind such a network sees markets and can run simulated agents with no configuration at all. Placing live orders still needs a network that reaches the venue directly.
- **Data controls**: the optional data-sharing choices are answered during onboarding, the full notices are readable inside the app with no network, and a new Data Controls section in Settings withdraws any of them at any time.

**Improvements**

- **Waiting is legible**: a reply in progress shows a live elapsed time, and a message queued behind the agent's current turn now says so instead of showing nothing at all.
- **Threads that say what they are about**: a conversation is named automatically from its first exchange and each row carries a preview of your opening line, so the list no longer reads as a column of identical entries. The target chip shows the agent's name, and switching target opens a fresh thread rather than relabelling one addressed to someone else.
- **A P&L chart you can break down**: total, realized, unrealized and the return on capital currently in positions are now selectable on the chart, with the headline, axis and tooltip all following the selection, rather than being buried in a tooltip.
- **A credit reading that fits**: large balances are shortened in the chat composer so the strip keeps its shape, with a shortcut beside it to where credit is bought — the panel and the purchase log keep every decimal.
- **Topic lists admit a failed read**: when the topic list or its preview cannot be fetched, that is now stated plainly, instead of an empty row implying the venue has no topics.
- **A calmer console**: wallets no longer attached to an agent fold into one collapsed group, the conversation list starts collapsed so the sections beneath it stay reachable, and long explanations next to a switch move behind a question-mark badge.
- **A restart you can always reach**: Settings now carries a standing restart for the local runtime, instead of offering one only after a change that happened to need it, and it waits until the runtime answers again before returning you to the dashboard.
- **Fewer decisions in the agent form**: the position limit and the minimum order size are no longer edited there — both are still recorded and still enforced on every order at every autonomy level — and the adversarial second-opinion review, which every creation path already turned off, is gone from the form too.
- **The window opens the way you set it**: interface size is applied before the first frame instead of snapping a moment later, and the default window is larger.
- **The bundled momentum breakout playbook judges what it can actually see**: its breakout tests now read order-book depth and liquidity trends, and require confirmation held across two observations at least fifteen minutes apart, instead of asking for traded volume and price history that no agent tool reports.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed scheduled turns being written off when the connection to the model dropped mid-request: a dropped connection is retried now, where before it ended the turn outright.
- Fixed whole classes of two-outcome market — up or down, over or under, one team against another — being skipped during discovery and refused at order time: each is now read as a yes/no pair with the venue's own wording kept alongside, so the agent knows which side it is judging.
- Fixed a turn hanging for hours when the connection carried keep-alive traffic but no content — one run sat for over nine hours under a three-minute idle limit — because any traffic at all reset that limit; only real progress resets it now.
- Fixed simulated agents created from the fleet screen or from a topic waking, thinking, and then parking every order for approval: a simulated agent starts on Autopilot wherever it was created, as the onboarding wizard already did.
- Fixed the final step of onboarding failing with a locked-wallet message, and no field to answer it with, for anyone who spent more than an hour reading the consent notices: the session no longer expires part-way through the wizard, and the refusal is shown in your own language.
- Fixed agents on Windows that woke but never acted, or stopped waking at all: a fault while saving autonomy state, or inside a scheduler tick, no longer takes down the timer that wakes the agent, and an autonomy record that cannot be read is reported with a recovery hint instead of leaving the agent silent.
- Fixed a factory reset that could not finish leaving the app unable to start at all, with every relaunch failing the same way; a blocked wipe is now reported and start-up carries on.
- Fixed the send icon missing from the chat composer in the installed app, where it rendered as an empty box.
- Fixed re-importing a recovery phrase opening on an empty console: creating a wallet used to delete every agent record, including those belonging to the phrase being imported. Agents are retired rather than deleted now, and the Agents screen points at the ones the phrase can restore.
- Fixed the Account panel asking on every launch what to do about a credit account left behind on a previous recovery phrase; the answer is remembered against that particular pair of accounts, while a genuinely new one can still ask.
- Fixed a brand-new agent sitting idle until the next scheduled interval: it now wakes as soon as the last setting that makes it runnable is in place.
- Fixed the outcome of redeeming a code, and of saving an agent's configuration, being reported a screen away from the button that triggered it, which read as a dead click; both report next to their own control now.
- Fixed deleting a wallet leaving the account that holds your credit unrecoverable: the next unlock signed into a new, empty account instead of the existing one, which stopped agents waking and position monitoring with them.

[Downloads for 0.1.9](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.9)

## 0.1.8 — 2026-08-21

**New features**

- **Gas for your first credit purchase, handled automatically**: a main wallet holding only the billing token used to hit a dead end when buying credit, because the one-time approval it has to send needs a little chain gas — the app now requests that gas itself, waits for it to land and only then completes the purchase. Both the desktop app and the command line warn up front that the wait can take a minute or two.
- **A preview of what your topics actually match**: an agent's configuration screen now shows how many live markets its saved topics match right now, up to the discovery limit, and says so plainly when the answer is none — so a filter that quietly matches nothing is visible before the agent next wakes, rather than after a silent round.

**Improvements**

- **Transaction hashes you can check**: every hash on the wallet and account screens — sends, swaps, transfer and swap history, credit purchases — now links straight to the explorer for the chain the transaction was actually on, instead of leaving you to copy the string out by hand.
- **A sign-in prompt where you will actually see it**: whenever the app is signed out — after importing a different key, for instance — a dismissible banner now says so from anywhere in the app, and names the reason when the session cannot come back on its own. The account panel explains in one line why unlocking the wallet did not restore it.
- **A clearer topic picker**: the two topic levels are now labelled for what they do, pinned markets have their own block instead of sitting inside the topics card, and a running count of what is selected is shown. The free-text tag box is gone — a typo there was silently accepted and only surfaced much later as a topic nothing could resolve.
- **Tidier wallet balances**: a gas balance too small to cover even one approval is now hidden when the wallet also holds a token balance, so a wallet that is ready to spend no longer looks as though it still needs more gas bought.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed an agent judging markets well outside the topics it was given: the two topic levels were being merged into one either/or list, so a crypto agent with short-horizon sub-tags could be handed US-equity markets. A market must now match a level-1 topic and, when level-2 tags are set, one of those too — narrowing the selection rather than widening it. Existing agents keep their old behaviour until their topics are saved again.
- Fixed paper-trading agents reporting "invalid bearer token" and no paper account after a new key was imported or a new agent was added: a paper account is now created automatically at start-up, on unlock and when an agent is added, and an account that is already in use is never replaced.
- Fixed a performance curve showing money that belonged to a wallet which had since been replaced: balances are no longer sampled while the wallet is locked, and a failed balance read now leaves an honest gap in the chart instead of repeating the last known value.
- Fixed saving on an agent's skills tab appearing to do nothing: because Save sits at the foot of a long list of toggles, the confirmation was scrolling off-screen at the top of the page. It now appears next to the Save button that produced it.
- Fixed saved level-1 topics briefly being marked as not listed by the venue while the topic list was still loading — clicking one in that state removed a perfectly live topic.

[Downloads for 0.1.8](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.8)

## 0.1.7 — 2026-08-19

**New features**

- **Swap on your own wallet**: the wallet screen gains a swap that buys the billing token with the gas coin already sitting on the wallet, in a single on-chain trade with a live quote and a stated minimum — you receive at least that much or the trade reverts and costs only gas. It is signed locally, the tokens land on the same address that paid, and every swap is logged with its transaction hash.
- **Bring back a deleted agent**: importing a recovery phrase now lists the agents that phrase has owned, and restoring one re-declares it on its original wallet with its balances, receipts and history reattached — none of it had been erased. Restored agents come back on the paper exchange with default settings, since custom instructions and limits were never part of the record.

**Improvements**

- **Agent wallets that any wallet app recognises**: each agent's wallet is now the same address a standard wallet app derives for the matching account of that recovery phrase, so any agent wallet can be opened, inspected or swept from MetaMask with no special handling. The main wallet is unchanged.
- **Credit that no longer cuts a run in half**: a run is no longer stopped dead the moment the balance reaches zero — it is allowed to finish, and the balance may go negative — and if it stays negative every agent is stopped with a banner explaining why, leaving the resume as your own deliberate step after topping up.
- **One address to fund on a fresh install**: the first agent created on a brand-new recovery phrase now sits on the same wallet that pays for credit, instead of the app presenting two unrelated addresses to fund.
- **A way out of an out-of-credit failure**: runs that failed for the one cause a retry cannot fix — the account having no credit left — now carry an add-credit link straight to the account settings, in the feed, the agent activity list and the run detail alike.
- **A clearer skill install**: the install button now shows activity while a skill is downloaded, checked and installed rather than appearing to do nothing for several seconds, and catalogue rows drop the empty "unverified · 0 installs · 0 stars" line — the trust caution now appears in the install dialog, at the moment the decision is actually made.
- **Which side the money bought**: earnings rows now lead with the outcome each entry was on, and list every side when a market was entered on more than one, instead of leaving it to be dug out of an expanded row.
- **One address fewer to look after**: the separate sign-in address is retired — whatever sits on it is now spendable as an ordinary agent wallet, so the wallet screen no longer shows it, nor the one-off migration step it used to need.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed the Linux packages failing at first launch with a missing-runtime error: the bundled runtime is now staged into the Linux builds as it always was on macOS and Windows.
- Fixed the recovery-phrase backup prompt being forgotten: whether a phrase has been written down is now recorded alongside the wallet itself, so an operator who wipes an install and creates a second wallet is prompted to back up the new phrase instead of unknowingly holding one that exists only as encrypted data on the machine.
- Fixed a newly created wallet inheriting the deleted one's world: it no longer shows the old phrase's recoverable-funds rows, no longer adopts its paper-exchange account and profit curve, and no longer starts up with position protection halted by a days-old emergency stop. Purchase, transfer and run history now read back scoped to the wallet you actually hold, and the previous account is signed out.
- Deleting a wallet now returns you to onboarding instead of stranding you on a wallet screen whose wallet is gone, and the passphrase is the only gate: the old flow told you to lock the wallet first and then appeared to ask you to unlock it again.
- Fixed stop-losses and protective sells being silently switched off while every agent still read as running: the halt is now reported in a banner with a one-click resume.
- Fixed an account with no credit left producing an error card every few seconds and burning several of the day's run reservations in a single wake: a run that failed for a cause no retry can fix now ends that wake, and the next scheduled interval retries once — the cadence you configured.
- Fixed paper-exchange markets that have not begun trading being reported as having a payout to claim, which also filled the log with settlement warnings about data the venue never published; a market with no order book is now labelled as such and stays visible as an untraded holding.
- Fixed a first credit purchase failing immediately after its spending approval had plainly succeeded: the purchase now waits for the approval to be visible to the billing side before signing, and refuses outright — having signed nothing — if it still is not.
- Fixed the app capitalising and autocorrecting text you type into it, so a confirmation phrase you are asked to type exactly is no longer altered as you type it.

[Downloads for 0.1.7](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.7)

## 0.1.6 — 2026-08-17

**Improvements**

- **Activity history that ends where the venue ends**: "Load older entries" on an agent's venue activity now keeps walking back until the venue itself has nothing older to give, instead of stopping at a fixed number of rows. Past the first screenful that feed also refreshes more slowly — it is being read as history rather than watched live — and pulling in older entries no longer reloads the rest of the tab.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed agents repeatedly re-examining holdings on markets that had already finished: whether a market is over is now decided by the venue that settles it, rather than inferred from a discovery listing or from the paper exchange's own simulation, so settled holdings stay out of review and exit rounds instead of being offered up again on every wake and then failing to price for want of an order book. The summary of holdings an agent is given now follows the same rule, where before it counted every position held — including the large share it had no way to trade — and so described a book far bigger than the one it could act on.
- Fixed a predict.fun agent finding no candidate markets at all until its market list had finished its first sync after start-up, whenever its strategy limits how far ahead a market may close: this venue publishes the closing date on the topic rather than on the individual market, and the live listing is now joined to it, so dated markets are no longer all rejected as undated with nothing to explain it. predict.fun positions also carry their market's closing date for the first time.
- Fixed the Earnings tab stating a profit for a market whose purchase is no longer within reach of the loaded history, which overstated results — on one live account by several thousand dollars. Such a market is now flagged with no profit figure and a neutral verdict instead of a win or a loss, and is left out of the header total along with a count of what was excluded, under a footnote saying how far back the figures actually see.
- Fixed credit prices, the purchase confirmation and the auto top-up limits always being labelled in USDC: they now name the token the billing network in use actually charges in. Purchases always settled in the correct token — only the label was wrong.

[Downloads for 0.1.6](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.6)

## 0.1.5 — 2026-08-16

**New features**

- **Bring an existing wallet in**: a seed phrase can now be imported during first-run setup, and a machine that already holds a wallet can replace it from the wallet screen's danger zone, where the phrase is validated while the current wallet is still intact. Setup also resumes cleanly on an install whose agents outlived their wallet — it says how many agents it found, warns that their addresses re-derive from the phrase just entered, and stops offering new ones at the limit.
- **The facts behind every position**: expanding a position now shows what the shares still held cost, when the agent opened it, every order behind it and the reasoning that led to it, with a link into the run that decided it. The earnings view adds the shares bought over a market's whole life and the weighted average price they were bought at.
- **A date window on the history views**: the order and earnings logs can be narrowed to any range up to a month, and on the order log the window narrows the totals and page count with it, so the pager no longer offers twenty pages of a three-row result.

**Improvements**

- **Topic pickers that match what the venue actually carries**: the topic and sub-topic chips are now read live from the venue instead of a hand-kept list, so dead tags are gone, the venue's biggest categories — the major sports leagues, box office — are finally offered, and a chip that would discover nothing is never shown. Sub-topic chips now toggle off as well as on, and every selected topic is listed in an editable box below, including one typed by hand.
- **Holdings review moved to its own pass**: open positions are reviewed on a separate wake, a few at a time oldest-first, so an agent holding a large book no longer spends most of a trading turn re-reading its own positions and hitting its per-turn token limit. That pass can still close a position, through exactly the same approval and order checks as any other trade.
- **Standing explanations behind a ? badge**: the evergreen notes that used to push controls down the page now sit behind a ? beside the label they explain, while everything that depends on the moment — errors, warnings, empty states and money or irreversible-action notices — stays in plain view.
- **Timestamps you can read**: the order and earnings logs print the date and clock time with the relative age beneath, so last month no longer reads as "912h ago"; earnings rows are sorted by recency by default and now show a visible expand cue for the detail panel they had all along.
- **The full activity history on the paper exchange**: the activity feed no longer stops at the newest 200 entries — older entries load on demand behind a button, and the earnings view sums everything reachable rather than a truncated slice.
- **Logs say why an agent stopped waking**: a paused agent, a tripped kill switch and a saved schedule state that cannot be read each announce themselves once, instead of producing no output at all, so a stalled agent no longer looks exactly like an idle one.
- **Evidence scoped to the market being judged**: the built-in evidence source is now asked about the exact market under judgment rather than its broad topic, so what comes back bears on the decision at hand. Installs configured before this are updated on start-up, and a source you had customised is left untouched and reported rather than quietly rewritten.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed a position that had gained value becoming impossible to sell: the per-order limit now bounds only how much new exposure a buy may take on, while closing is bounded by the position itself, so a one-click close no longer fails with a size error — and the more a position gained, the more stuck it used to be.
- Fixed markets with an unusably wide spread being researched and judged in full before the order was refused: the pre-trade book check works again for paper and Polymarket agents, and the local market list now records both sides of the book, so a wide market is dropped from the shortlist before a turn is spent on it.
- Markets the venue has stopped listing are now removed from the local market list once their absence is confirmed, instead of lingering with a stale close time and liquidity and being picked again and again; a failure to reach the venue still keeps the market, so one bad minute cannot drain a healthy pool.
- Fixed settled markets on the paper exchange being re-offered for position review on every wake, where the agent could neither price nor close them: a settled holding is now recognised as no longer tradeable and skipped, and it is flagged in the positions listing, so a holding left stranded on a market the exchange closed without settling can still be spotted.
- Fixed paper agents being refused at the last step with a book-unreadable error on markets nobody had traded yet, after a full research and judgment turn had already been paid for: paper orders are now priced and checked against the live public market book, and the paper exchange's own readiness surfaces as an order-time error with an accurate reason.
- Fixed the recorded profit-and-loss curve over-reporting profit on paper accounts with long histories: cash flow is now read from account balances, which are complete, rather than walked back through a history the exchange truncates and eventually purges.
- Fixed one failing topic taking a whole discovery round down with it: each selected topic now fails on its own and is reported, instead of a single error from the venue emptying that round's entire candidate list.
- Fixed a wallet balance that was still loading looking exactly like one that had finished: the on-chain balance line now shows that it is fetching instead of sitting motionless in the same muted grey as the notes around it.
- Fixed the transfer wording in Traditional Chinese and Vietnamese, where the send flow read as submitting a form and as depositing money rather than transferring funds out.

[Downloads for 0.1.5](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.5)

## 0.1.4 — 2026-08-15

**New features**

- **Five languages, all the way through**: the interface now speaks English, Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Malay, switchable from the top bar, from settings, or from the first-run screen — and the chosen language reaches the agent too, so its analysis and verdicts come back in the language being read rather than in English.
- **Three agents instead of one**: an install can now run up to three agents side by side, each with its own wallet, schedule and limits.
- **Add and remove agents without a restart**: creating an agent used to mean restarting the runtime before anything would actually wake it. A new agent is now registered and scheduled in place, and removing one shuts its schedule down the same way.
- **Entries are a direction and a size, not a probability guess**: an agent now states which side it is taking and picks one of three size tiers, resolved against the real account balance. The old test — the agent's estimated probability against the market price — turned out to be restating the price back, passing nearly every market it looked at while opening almost nothing.
- **A resting order when the spread is too wide to cross**: agents now see the real bid and ask, and an entry refused for crossing too wide a spread can be placed as a resting limit order instead of being dropped, then swept away if it has not filled within the strategy's window.
- **A price confirmation before any credit purchase**: buying credit now opens a confirmation that reads the price back — the exact sum on the button being clicked, and the credits it adds — so funds only move once it has been confirmed. The redeem-a-code field also moved to the top of the account screen, where a new install is actually looking.

**Improvements**

- **One topic per run, several runs per wake**: a run used to be handed up to ten unrelated markets and re-sent all of that research at every step, so its cost grew with the square of the work it did. A run now takes a single event — at most two of its sub-markets — and a wake queues as many runs as its interval allows, so the same board gets worked through at a fraction of the tokens.
- **Near-identical bets no longer crowd out the real market**: exact-score, first-to-score, both-teams-to-score and halftime variants are dropped before they cost a research pass. One football match can list a dozen of them, and they were filling whole batches while the match's main market went unjudged.
- **Runaway turns stop themselves**: a turn now ends when it crosses its token ceiling and says so, distinctly from simply running out of steps; a tool that keeps failing is set aside for the rest of the turn instead of being retried until the budget is gone; and a rate-limited read from the paper exchange is retried quietly rather than reaching the agent as a broken tool.
- **Switching between agents is instant**: agent pages used to blank out and re-fetch everything on every switch, which on a few days of history meant a visible stall — and, briefly, the previous agent's positions under the new agent's name. Each page now keeps its own last-seen data, and the repeated position reads behind it are shared.
- **The per-order limit trims instead of refusing**: an order above the limit is now reduced to the limit and submitted, rather than blocked or parked for an approval that nobody answered. A second, configured exposure ceiling has been retired — it blocked every further order once a book grew close to it, regardless of the cash actually available — leaving order size bounded by the real account balance.
- **An activity feed that shows what happened**: a discovery sweep passes on nearly everything it looks at, and those rows used to bury the few judgments that acted, so the feed now lists only the ones that did — the full set is still in the run's decision trace. A blocked order shows the gate's verdict plus a counted list of the objections instead of one long red paragraph.
- **Plain language where machine text used to be**: a run's sources now say what a call did and what it asked for, in local time, instead of printing tool ids and raw parameters; the built-in research source reads as a web search rather than as an unfamiliar name; and in the translated interfaces a verdict now reads as the agent's own action — an order placed, or none — rather than as something about the market.
- **The wallet's lock state is legible**: a run skipped for a locked wallet now leads with the state and what to do about it, and a locked wallet offers an unlock dialog where the reminder used to merely point at settings. Every lock and unlock is also recorded as it happens, including the passive one when a signing session expires, rather than only at start-up.
- **Malay, Indonesian and Vietnamese read like the product**: many dictionary-correct but wrong-domain words were rewritten — a credit balance no longer reads as a home loan, a transaction hash no longer as minced meat — and the per-order approval mode now says plainly that each order needs approval instead of borrowing an aviation metaphor.
- **Topics can be changed after an agent exists**: what an agent looks at was previously fixed at creation, for the agent's whole life; it now sits in the agent's own configuration alongside its other settings.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed being left signed in with no usable account key, and no way back, after an update moved the service endpoints: the old key was presented to a server that had never issued it, rejected, and then discarded as invalid. A stale key is now cleared along with the endpoints it belonged to, and signing in again lands on the same account.
- Fixed automatic top-up switching itself off permanently the first time anything went wrong — a rate-limited quote, a briefly unreachable billing host, a momentarily short wallet — which in practice meant it never ran at all. Only failures that happen before a payment can possibly have started are retried; anything else still stops and waits for a look, and the reason it stopped now survives a restart.
- Fixed automatically sized orders that could not succeed: the size was derived from a configured exposure ceiling instead of the real balance, so a "small" order could come out several times larger than the account, and the resulting amount often carried more decimal places than the venue accepts, failing the same order on every retry. Sizes now read the live balance, are rounded down to whole cents, and a balance that cannot be read blocks the order instead of falling back to the ceiling.
- Fixed a single market-listing call being able to spend a whole turn's token budget before any research had happened — over 600,000 input tokens on a large board. Agents no longer list the board themselves: every wake already sweeps the entire filtered pool and hands the agent the market to judge.
- Fixed markets being researched in full and then refused at the final gate: the pre-research screen was reading a cached market list that carries no order book and prices that can be days out of date, so it never screened anything out. It now reads the live book, and shares the same spread rule as the gate so the two cannot disagree.
- Fixed a newly created agent that failed to register with the paper exchange reporting success: the error was written to a screen the app immediately navigated away from, leaving an agent that could not trade, read its own balance or show one row of history behind three empty tabs. That failure now stays on screen and names what to run to fix it.
- Fixed switching an agent's strategy playbook doing nothing observable: confirming the switch changed only which skills were allowed and left the agent bound to the previous playbook. The dialog now completes the switch, or refuses with a reason on the spot, and the list is grouped so the one-playbook-plus-add-ons rule is visible before choosing.
- Fixed a Buy click on an unfunded wallet reading as dead: the refusal appeared in a shared message line several screens below the button. It now appears at the button, and points at the wallet screen where the deposit address lives.
- Fixed the new-agent screen offering to share a wallet already held by another agent — a choice that could only ever fail on save. Each new agent takes the next wallet nobody holds.
- Fixed an open order's market title always linking to Polymarket, whichever venue the order was placed on, and a paper market's title not linking at all.
- Fixed a run ending in a screen of markup instead of a conclusion when the model service folded its own tool-call syntax into the answer; the turn now fails with a single sentence and echoes none of it.
- Fixed long-context turns being killed as dead connections after a minute of quiet from the model service: the silence deadline is now three minutes, so a turn carrying a large transcript is no longer cut off while the answer is still coming.
- Fixed order receipts printing a broken percentage where the agent gave no estimate, and $0 for an automatically sized order that failed before it was priced. Recognised venue rejections are also stated in plain language now, with the original text kept in the tooltip, since the receipt is the record.
- Fixed resuming after an emergency close-out leaving agents that had been running autonomously switched off, with nothing anywhere recording that they ever had been. Resume now restores autonomy for exactly those agents, and both resume dialogs say what they will restore.

[Downloads for 0.1.4](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.4)

## 0.1.3 — 2026-08-14

**New features**

- **Trade cards name the exact market they bought**: a card now shows the parent event above the specific line an agent traded, so a bet on one leg of a multi-market event — or on a line whose own title names neither side of a match — can be identified at a glance, across approvals, orders, positions and past judgments.

**Improvements**

- **The whole order history, not just the newest slice**: history is now paged as you browse, so every receipt on the machine is reachable instead of only the most recent couple of hundred, and the tab badge and status filters count the full log rather than that window.
- **Failures said in plain language**: a failed run now names the cause an operator can act on where it is recognisable — credit, credentials, a content filter, reachability, a timeout — instead of printing the raw error text, and the original wording is still there in the run's trace.
- **A proper launch screen**: starting the app now shows a branded welcome instead of a grey "loading…", and it clears as soon as the app is ready rather than holding you for a fixed wait.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed installing a skill pinned to a specific version failing outright: every pinned install was refused, whatever version was named, and those installs now go through.

[Downloads for 0.1.3](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.3)

## 0.1.2 — 2026-08-13

**New features**

- **Credit at a glance on every screen**: how much credit is left, and how far through it you are, now sits in the corner of every route — tinted amber when the balance is running low and red when it is overdrawn. Drag it clear if it covers something you need; it steps aside on the Account screen, where the full ledger already answers the question properly.
- **A second bundled playbook**: an experimental strategy now ships beside the default one, entering on source-backed conviction rather than an arithmetic edge bar — at least two independent sources, estimates acted on at the lower bound, a written case against every judgment, and long shots banned outright while the favourite side stays buyable. Everything else about it is deliberately identical to the default playbook, so the two can be run side by side on paper.
- **Skill links open in the app**: clicking a NeoTrade link to a skill now brings the window forward and lands on the marketplace with that skill already searched for. Installing it still takes an explicit click on that row's own button.

**Improvements**

- **A test build can no longer touch your real one**: the beta channel now installs as its own application, under its own name, with its own encrypted keystore, settings and records — so a beta session can no longer read or overwrite the state of a live install, and both can run at the same time.
- **Profit and loss leads with the percentage**: the Dashboard and each agent's Overview now headline the ratio and put the dollar figure on the line below, because +$4.00 says nothing until you know the size of the book behind it. The token-count tiles are gone from both strips — spend is accounted for in the Account panel's charge list, in the unit it is actually billed in.
- **A trace opens on what you clicked**: opening a trace from a receipt or a judgment now narrows to that one market and lands on the section the row belongs to, with a way back out to the whole turn.
- **Skills that say what they are**: every row on an agent's Skills tab now carries the skill's version, origin and market alongside its description, so choosing a strategy is no longer a choice between five near-identical names.
- **Your account is keyed to the main wallet**: points, credit and the profile card now sit on the address that actually pays and trades, and existing accounts move across without losing their history. If that move cannot complete, the reason is now stated in the Account panel and from the command line, instead of sitting only in a log file.
- **A funded wallet only ever signs a real sign-in**: before the main wallet signs a platform sign-in challenge, the message must parse as a standard sign-in request, name this app, and be addressed to that wallet — so an impersonated or compromised endpoint cannot turn a login into a trading session.
- **Money in and money out, separately**: the wallet screen now splits incoming from outgoing, each in its own section with its own record.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed an agent quietly going silent after the strategy it is bound to was switched off in its own permitted-skills list: that row can no longer be unchecked, changing strategy now adds the new playbook beside the bound one and walks you through the swap, and the Strategy tab keeps its repair controls on screen when a binding is broken rather than showing only an error.
- Fixed agents created outside the first-run wizard starting with no research sources subscribed while the Config screen labelled that state "Default" — which could leave an agent parked indefinitely. New agents now subscribe the house evidence source, and a source list you saved yourself is never rewritten.
- Fixed a real points balance reading as 0 on the profile card; the correct figure is now read, and a read that fails shows a dash instead of a zero, since "could not be read" and "earned nothing" are very different answers.
- Fixed installing a skill from the marketplace failing on Windows with a missing-unzip error: archives are now unpacked with whichever tool the machine actually ships, and if none works the message names what was tried.
- Fixed Windows paths being rejected as not absolute when adding a skill from a local folder or declaring a script-backed research source — drive-letter and network paths are now accepted, not just Unix-style ones.
- Fixed a paper-exchange position resting on the market's lowest price being impossible to sell: the exit price is now moved up to the nearest price the venue can express instead of the order being refused. Buys are unaffected, since rounding a buy up would spend more than was authorised.
- Fixed paper agents entering on almost no edge and piling into long shots, which in live paper runs bled the bankroll on cheap tails and spread crossing. The paper preset no longer loosens the minimum edge, the size cap or the price band — only how widely and how often an agent looks — and values still sitting at the old preset numbers move with it, while anything you set yourself stays.
- Fixed dates and times printing in the machine's own locale in the middle of English tables, so timestamps now read the same way everywhere in the app.

[Downloads for 0.1.2](https://github.com/NeoSoul-AI/neotrade-release/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.2)

## 0.1.1 — 2026-08-12

**New features**

- **predict.fun joins Polymarket and the paper exchange**: agents can now trade on predict.fun, with a funding view of its own — the deposit address and chain, the gas balance, the exchange approvals and any redeemable winnings — and one install can run agents on different venues side by side.
- **Strategies you can bind, read and tune**: every trading agent now runs a named strategy playbook whose parameters are on screen and editable, separated into hard fences a deterministic check enforces and guidance the model is only asked to follow. Three playbooks ship: a general baseline, one for markets resolving soon, and one for momentum and breakouts.
- **A decision trace for every run**: each run is recorded end to end — the trigger, every tool call and research lookup, the judgment, the challenge to it, the deterministic gate's arithmetic, the approval and the resulting order — and reads back as a plain-language timeline whose sources are clickable links rather than raw output.
- **A profit and loss curve that survives a restart**: the dashboard and each agent's overview now chart recorded history over the last day, week or month, with the banked part and the part still held labelled separately, and a break in recording drawn as a break instead of bridged over.
- **Sell everything and stop, in one action**: any position can be closed from its own row, and a single control sells the whole book, redeems what the venue allows and stops the agent — on your own authority, so it waits neither for the agent's next turn nor for an approval you would only be granting yourself.
- **Take-profit sells that rest on the book**: an agent can park a priced sell as a target rather than only closing at the market, and an immediate close-out supersedes any target resting on that position, so parked shares can never shield it from a stop.
- **A house account for the model and the evidence feed**: sign in with your wallet instead of pasting an API key, then see the credit balance, what a single analysis costs and where the spend went, buy more credit on-chain, and optionally arm an auto top-up bounded by a floor you set and a rolling daily cap.
- **A reserve for running costs**: an amount you choose is held back from the main wallet's reported balance so agents never trade the money that pays for the model and the evidence feed, and the account screen says so when trading crosses into it.
- **Send funds out of any trading wallet**: a send flow with a live quote, a maximum that leaves enough behind for gas and an outcome in plain words — plus a history of every send and every credit purchase, so a transaction hash is still there after the dialog is closed.
- **An earnings view per market**: settled markets that drop off the positions list stay visible with what went in and what came back, and each row expands to the agent's own reasoning and the venue's entries behind it.
- **Reviews for positions nobody has looked at**: a strategy can set a review interval, after which the agent is woken about holdings that nothing has re-judged. It decides what to do with them — nothing instructs it to close.
- **Points and a profile card**: the top bar carries your profile and the points earned across your wallets, with a way through to the leaderboard.
- **Update notices at launch**: the app checks for a new version at startup and names it in a dismissible banner. Installing stays a deliberate click, because it stops the runtime that may be holding an unlocked wallet mid-order.

**Improvements**

- **A first run that ends in the console**: three steps — the passphrase that encrypts the wallet, an optional redemption code and sign-in, then the agent — and the wallet is left unlocked at the end, instead of dropping you behind a "wallet locked" banner seconds after you typed the passphrase.
- **Unlock once**: unlocking no longer asks how long the session should last; keys stay unlocked until you lock the app or quit it.
- **A locked wallet no longer costs a whole analysis**: the run is skipped at the start with a reason, rather than researching and judging only to be refused at signing, and it recovers by itself on the next tick after you unlock. A manual run refuses up front instead of reporting success.
- **The runtime picks itself back up**: an unexpected death of the background runtime is followed by a respawn with backoff, and the window reconnects to the fresh one.
- **A lapsed account session can be recovered**: unlocking the wallet now signs a session back in after it has already expired, instead of only renewing one that was still alive — which was the case that needed it least.
- **A more legible interface**: every small text size moves up a step, and the wallet screen, agent configuration and add-source panels use the width of the window instead of stopping halfway across it.
- **A refreshed look**: a new app icon across every platform, a palette keyed to the product's own cyan, and the wordmark in the sidebar.
- **Plainer words in the feeds**: verdicts read "traded" and "no trade", the permanent "registered" badge is gone, and per-market earnings read "put in" and "came back" rather than mixing direction with exit route. The log and the command line now name a market instead of printing its 66-character id.
- **Feeds behind tabs**: the agent's own record and the venue's activity sit behind tabs, as do the dashboard's activity and pending approvals, so the second of each is no longer invisible once the first grows — and approvals waiting on a person carry a count badge.
- **A skill marketplace you can act on**: the catalogue is filtered to trading-relevant entries with a way to show the rest, installing from a local folder uses the native picker, and a refused install is reported inside the row it was refused for instead of in a banner below the whole page.
- **Credit stated in one unit**: the account screen and the command line now give house credit in credits, with purchase prices left in the coin you actually sign for and the credit value shown beside them.
- **Less leaves the machine to earn points**: the volume report no longer sends the side, size, price or value of a fill — every money figure is derived on-chain instead — so no edited client can inflate what it earns.

**Bug fixes**

- Fixed a filled order being recorded as a total non-fill on predict.fun: a page of the order list was re-served indefinitely, so a just-placed order sitting behind older account history was never found and its fill was logged as zero.
- Fixed an agent re-answering its very first turn forever: each run now starts from a clean transcript, rather than loading a snapshot that had accumulated the prompts and none of the answers.
- Fixed a long-running analysis being swept away and restarted while it was still working, leaving two runs racing on one agent.
- Fixed paper agents judging market after market and never placing an order: a paper agent's entry thresholds are now loosened along with its spending limits, instead of being left at real-money settings.
- Fixed a resting sell priced at or below the best bid liquidating a position instead of parking a target, and a refused close destroying that position's take-profit and then executing nothing — leaving it with neither a stop nor a target.
- Fixed being unable to move an agent back to paper: the open-positions check counted positions from the wrong venue, so an agent that had switched to a real-money venue and changed its mind was told about twelve positions it did not hold there, and a refused switch stopped it trading rather than leaving it where it was. Leaving a real-money venue with open positions is still refused.
- Fixed a credit payment that had in fact gone through being left on screen as unconfirmed with "do not buy again": the app now follows the payment up and updates once the server settles it. A purchase turned away by rate limiting is also reported as never submitted, rather than as money that may have moved.
- Fixed one deposit QR code standing in for every venue and captioned for the wrong network: each wallet now shows the address, asset and chain that would actually credit it, and a paper wallet says outright that nothing sent there is credited.
- Fixed the app capitalising and autocorrecting what you type — agent names, addresses, market and model ids and redemption codes are left exactly as typed. A go-live confirmation was being refused for a name the field had silently capitalised, with nothing on screen saying why.
- Fixed a failed run showing a red badge over a timeline of uniformly green steps with the reason nowhere in the app, and a request refused by a content filter now says so instead of sending you to audit a key, a balance and a model name that were never the cause.
- Fixed the bundled evidence source answering every lookup with nothing in it, so agents reasoned without the evidence they appeared to have consulted; existing installs are repaired at startup. A search tool is also no longer offered to an agent with no search source configured, where every call it made was a guaranteed failure.
- Fixed the market list being empty or stale for the first interval after every start — exactly when an agent is most likely to wake and find nothing to trade.
- Fixed markets on a venue that does not publish liquidity being hidden from every agent, with no setting that could let them through, and only the first twenty markets on predict.fun being visible at all.
- Fixed earnings overstating profit by dropping what a position cost to enter: a $300 buy-in redeemed for $1,578.94 reported the entire payout as profit.
- Fixed the agents list showing a green "running" pill for an agent that had just been stopped.
- Fixed order history listing the same blocked or failed order two, three or four times over — once per restart.
- Fixed one agent's positions failing to load because of an error raised by a venue that agent has nothing to do with.
- Fixed a wallet reporting itself unlocked while every order was refused at signing, with the decrypted keys left resident in memory.
- Fixed agents staying idle after the machine woke from sleep, and a Windows install or uninstall running over a live app leaving one file behind and a half-applied install with nothing said about it.
- Fixed the add-credit panel reporting a broken catalogue when the server simply sells no membership packages, which hid the credit bundles it did send. A Buy click during a payment, or with a locked wallet, now says what is in the way instead of doing nothing silently.
- Fixed a sign-in failure being reported at the very bottom of the account screen, several screens away from the button that failed, which made the button read as dead.
- Fixed stopping the runtime from the command line appearing to hang until the model had finished answering; it now stops within ten seconds, and interrupting a second time exits immediately.
